answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-work admission: before an agent identity is accepted, its owner must solve a hash puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many identities share the same hardware fingerprint and funding address. One puzzle is cheap, like picking up an opal from a terrace, but minting a thousand identities means repeating the search a thousand times, so costs grow linearly while honest users pay once, like a single dune crosser. Attackers spend real electricity per fake peer; legitimate agents register quickly and vote with full weight.
